transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today?

I guess I’m here because my concentration has just gotten… not like it used to be. I work with loans and credit stuff, and I’ll be looking at a worksheet or a follow-up list for clients and realize I’ve read the same line three or four times and it still hasn’t really gone in.

And then I’ll put off making calls because even deciding what to do next feels harder than it should. It’s embarrassing, honestly. I used to be pretty good at keeping all those little details straight—my desk was never perfect, but I knew where things were, you know? Now I just kind of stare at things.
Have you noticed feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yes… I think so. Most days there’s this kind of dull heaviness with me. It’s not always crying or anything dramatic, it’s more like I’m carrying something around.

Even when I go to the community center, or I’m out in my garden—which used to really pick me up—I feel like I’m just moving through it. I’ll smile and say hello to people, pull weeds, water the plants… but inside it feels sort of flat, like I’m only pretending to enjoy it.
Have you had episodes like this before, or is this the first time you’ve felt this way?

It’s not really the first time I’ve felt sad, I mean everybody has rough spells, but this… this has been going on since my close friend died a little over two years ago.

She and I used to talk almost every day, and after she passed I kept thinking I’d sort of come back to myself, you know? Like after the services and all the calls and casseroles and people checking in… but it just kind of stayed with me. So, I’d say that’s when it started, a little over two years ago.
Since your friend passed away, have you experienced any periods where your mood improved even slightly for a few days, or has it been consistently heavy the entire time?

It’s been… mostly there since she died, a little over two years ago. I mean, I’m sure there were days when I was busy and maybe didn’t notice it as much—like when my sister came to visit, she always reorganizes my kitchen drawers, which drives me crazy—but the heaviness didn’t really go away.

It just kind of settled in after my friend passed, and I kept waiting for it to lift. It hasn’t, not really.
Since your friend passed away, have you found that things you used to enjoy, like gardening or spending time at the community center, no longer feel satisfying or pleasurable to you?

Yes… that’s a good way to put it. I still go to the community center, and I still work in my garden, because if I stop doing those things then I don’t know what I’d do with myself.

But most days there’s just this dull heaviness sitting with me. I’ll be pulling weeds or watering the tomatoes—well, I tried tomatoes last year and the squirrels got half of them, which was so annoying—and I’ll realize I’m not really enjoying it the way I used to. Same with the community center. I can smile and chat and act like I’m fine, but inside it feels like I’m just going through the motions with a smile pasted on.
Has there been a time when even the things you used to really enjoy, like gardening or seeing friends, didn’t feel good or rewarding to you at all?

Yes… I think so. Most days there’s this dull heaviness sitting with me, even when I’m doing things that used to make me feel better.

Like I’ll be at the community center, and people are talking and laughing, and I know I’m smiling back—probably too much, honestly, like when you’re trying not to make anyone ask what’s wrong—and then I’ll start thinking about whether I left the hose on in the garden or if I need to stop for milk, and… anyway. The point is, it doesn’t really feel rewarding. Same in the garden. I’m there, I’m doing it, but it’s like I’m just going through the motions with a smile pasted on.
Have you ever had a period when your mood was better for a few weeks or more, where you felt more like your usual self?

I don’t think so… not for a few weeks, no. Since my close friend died—just a little over two years ago now—it’s kind of been the same heaviness hanging around.

I mean, there are days where I’m distracted, like if I’m at work and someone brings in a stack of paperwork done completely wrong, or my neighbor starts telling me about her grandson’s soccer games in great detail… but that’s not the same as feeling like myself again. It hasn’t really lifted for any real stretch of time.
Have you found that you no longer take any pleasure or joy in things you used to enjoy, like gardening or seeing friends, even when you're doing them?

Yes… I still do them, you know, the garden and going to the community center, because they’re part of my routine. And honestly, if I don’t go, then people start asking where I’ve been, and then you have to explain yourself, and that becomes a whole thing.

But most days there’s this dull heaviness with me. Even when I’m somewhere that used to lift me up, like the garden or sitting with people at the center, it doesn’t really feel joyful. I can smile and talk and look like I’m enjoying myself, but inside it feels more like I’m just going through the motions with a smile pasted on.
Has there been a time recently when you felt absolutely no interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like gardening or seeing friends, even for a whole day or more?

Yes… I mean, I’m not sure I’d say “absolutely no” every second of the day, but most days there’s this dull heaviness sitting with me.

Like even if I go to the community center, or I’m out in the garden—those used to be the things that perked me up a little—I still feel like I’m just… doing what I’m supposed to do. Smiling, making small talk, pulling weeds, whatever it is. But it doesn’t really reach me. It’s more like going through the motions with a smile pasted on.
